interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The surgical findings included a Gleason 3+3 with tertiary pattern 4 (ISUP grade group 1), negative surgical margins, and no invasion of the seminal vesicles. The absence of lymph nodes removed and the finding of no lymphovascular invasion are favorable. Conversely, the preoperative PSA was elevated at 11.7. A key point of uncertainty is the nodal status, as no lymph nodes were removed, and missing nodal sampling widens this uncertainty. The biopsy findings showed a difference, with the second biopsy identifying perineural invasion, which contrasts with the initial finding. The postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical unknowns that would significantly revise this prognosis. The current horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 55 months without an event, reflecting the uncertainty inherent in the current data set. The fixed estimated horizon is 54.81 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 35.62–73.99 months; its coverage has not been validated.
